chapter: Harlem musicians and the road with Armstrong
title: Pops Foster, Barbarin and the Russell rhythm section
summary: Holmes praises Pops Foster and says a rhythm section should be felt rather than heard, comparing it to Sonny Greer in Ellington's band.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, then, did a lot of bass players come around to listen to Pops?

Everyone in New York come to listen to Pops. I don't know why, but they did. Yeah, he was very popular. Very popular. And he was a nice guy. Pops was really a nice guy. And I could understand why he become popular, because he was very nice.
And he was a very good bassist, too.
He was a very good bassist, and he loved to play his instrument.
Would you comment on the Luis Russell rhythm section? A lot of people have said it's one of the best rhythm sections ever.

Well, for what they were playing, the style of music they were playing, it was the best. Because they had a beat. I mean, you can't get away from it. They had a beat, you know. Strictly their own style.
And that must have helped the front line.
You had to pat your feet. What they say, if you can't pat your feet, it's not Jazz.
Well, now, would you say you were inspired by this kind of a rhythm section?

Oh, I loved it. Yes, indeed. Paul Barbarin. Boy, he... Nothin' flashy about it. But see, with a rhythm section, you're not supposed to hear it... Like drums and all of this technique... You're not supposed to hear the rhythm section. You're supposed to feel it. You're supposed to feel that rhythm. You're not supposed to hear it, a whole lot of bangin' and this-that-and-the-other. That's not a rhythm section. But it's supposed to inspire you, make you want to dance or do something, make you pat your feet, do something, move your fingers -- but move something. That's a rhythm section. Yeah, he had a wonderful rhythm section.

That's one thing I used to like about Duke's band, when Sonny Greer was in the band. Sonny was never acclaimed to be what you call a real star drummer, you know. But when he was with Duke's band, I don't care what other drummer Duke had or used in his band. None of them fit in the band like Sonny Greer did. Sonny had an old-fashioned beat, [SINGS IT], real jungle effect music. And it fit right into Duke's band. It just fit there. And when Sonny left the band, Duke tried out a whole lot of drummers, a whole lot of drummers, but none of them fit in the band like Sonny did.
It just didn't sound the same.
Well, that's the same way with Russell's rhythm section. The style of music he was playing, it couldn't be beat.
